# Counters

Every counter Cavalry has, from `counters.toml`, the single source ([ADR 0012](../decisions/0012-lay-out-the-counters-file.md)). The driver publishes each one in the [counters file](counters-file.md). A static counter is allocated when the file is created, in the record whose index is its id, and its label is its name. An instance counter is allocated per key when its instance is created, and its label is the name, a space, and the key's text as the doc column defines it. A `counter` never decreases while allocated; a `gauge` moves both ways. This page is generated by `scripts/gen-counters.py`: edit `counters.toml`, never this page, and `just lint-counters` fails when the two differ.

| Id | Name | Kind | Scope | What a change means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `counters.allocated` | gauge | static | Metadata records in the allocated state, this counter's own record included. |  |
| 1 | `counters.allocation_failed` | counter | static | Counter allocations refused because every record was in use: the counters file is full, and whatever needed the counter was refused with it. | Restart the driver with a larger counters file capacity; until then new publications and subscriptions are refused. |
| 2 | `publication.position` | gauge | instance | The producer position of one publication's log buffer, written by the driver on its duty cycle; key: correlation id (i64), session id (i32), stream id (i32), little-endian; label text: the three in decimal, space-separated. |  |
| 3 | `publication.limit` | gauge | instance | The position up to which one publication may write: the slowest subscriber's position plus the publication window, written by the driver; key and label as publication.position. | If publication.position sits at publication.limit, a subscriber is slow or stopped: compare the subscription.position counters of the stream and look at that subscriber. |
| 4 | `subscription.position` | gauge | instance | How far one subscription has read one publication's stream, written by the subscriber after each poll with a release store; key: correlation id (i64), session id (i32), stream id (i32), little-endian; label text: the three in decimal, space-separated. | A subscription.position that does not move while publication.position does is a subscriber that stopped polling; its publisher will be back-pressured when it reaches the window. |
| 5 | `publication.unblocked` | counter | static | Stale claims the driver turned into padding frames because a publisher claimed and did not commit within the unblock timeout (spec/log-buffer.md, The driver). | A publisher process died or stalled between claim and commit; find it from the publication whose position stopped moving, and keep claim and commit on one thread with nothing blocking between them. |
| 6 | `log_buffer.rejected_position` | counter | static | Subscriber positions the driver found outside the spec's bounds and refused to use; the client that wrote one is evicted (ADR 0010). | A client wrote an impossible position: a buggy binding or a hostile process. The driver's log names the client; rebuild or remove it. |
| 7 | `log_buffer.rejected_tail` | counter | static | Tail counters the driver found inconsistent with the active term count and refused to use; the publication is closed (ADR 0010). | A publisher wrote an impossible tail: a buggy binding or a hostile process. The driver's log names the publication; rebuild or remove the client. |
| 8 | `log_buffer.rejected_frame` | counter | static | Frames a subscriber found outside spec/frame.md's bounds in a term and reported; nothing after such a frame is delivered on that image. | A publisher wrote a corrupt frame, or a term was overwritten: check publication.unblocked and the driver's log for the publication. |
| 9 | `command_ring.unblocked` | counter | static | Padding records the driver wrote over a claim in the command ring that a client made and did not commit within the unblock timeout (spec/command-ring.md, Unblocking). | A client process died or stalled between claiming and committing a command; its own driver timeout closes it. If this repeats, find the client that keeps restarting and look at what stops it between claim and commit. |
| 10 | `command_ring.rejected_tail` | counter | static | Tail positions the driver found outside the command ring's bounds when it unblocked and refused to use (ADR 0010): the ring is corrupt and the driver reads nothing more from it (spec/command-ring.md, Unblocking). | A client wrote an impossible tail: a buggy binding or a hostile process, which the ring cannot name. Every client's commands now time out. Restart the driver, which recreates the ring; if the counter climbs again, stop clients one at a time until it stops, and look for a binding that was upgraded or does not conform to spec/command-ring.md. |
| 11 | `command_ring.rejected_record` | counter | static | Records the driver found outside the command ring's bounds, a length or type no client writes by the protocol (ADR 0010): the driver reads nothing more from the ring (spec/command-ring.md, Reading). | A client wrote a corrupt command: a buggy binding or a hostile process, which the ring cannot name. Every client's commands now time out. Restart the driver, which recreates the ring; if the counter climbs again, stop clients one at a time until it stops, and look for a binding that was upgraded or does not conform to spec/command-ring.md. |
| 12 | `client.timed_out` | counter | static | Clients the driver timed out because no command of theirs arrived within the client liveness timeout; their publications and subscriptions were removed and a client timeout event sent (spec/client-protocol.md, Liveness and timeouts). | A client stopped sending keepalives: it is stuck, paused under a debugger, or its conductor thread died. Its own driver timeout closes it. Find the process by the client id in the client timeout event and look at what stopped its conductor. |
| 13 | `client_protocol.rejected_command` | counter | static | Commands the driver decoded and refused: an unknown type, a message of the wrong length, a bad string, a channel that is not cavalry:ipc, or a client the driver had timed out (spec/client-protocol.md, What the driver rejects); the client got an error event when its correlation id was readable. | A client sent a command the protocol does not allow: a binding that does not conform to spec/client-protocol.md or was upgraded apart from the driver. The error event names the command; stop that client and check its version against the driver's. |
| 14 | `client_protocol.errors` | counter | static | Error events the driver sent, whatever the code: every command this version refused after the ring delivered it (spec/client-protocol.md, Error codes); the causes with a counter of their own are client_protocol.rejected_command, driver.registry_full and driver.log_create_failed. | Compare with client_protocol.rejected_command, driver.registry_full and driver.log_create_failed; an error none of them explains is code 2, 3 or 11, a client naming a registration the driver does not know, or a bug the error event's message names. |
| 15 | `driver.registry_full` | counter | static | Commands refused with error code 10 because the driver's registry of clients, publications, subscriptions or images, or the counters file, was at capacity (spec/client-protocol.md, Sizes). | A fixed capacity of the driver is reached: clients, publications or subscriptions are not being closed, or this host needs more than one driver's worth. Close what is not used; the error event's message names the registry; the capacities are the driver's in this version. |
| 16 | `driver.log_create_failed` | counter | static | Log buffers the driver could not create or size, refused with error code 12: the filesystem under the driver directory is full or not writable (spec/client-protocol.md, Commands). | Free space on the filesystem under the driver directory (/dev/shm on Linux): each cavalry:ipc publication needs 3 × 64 MiB + 4 KiB there while it is live or lingers. Close publications that are not used, or move the driver directory to a filesystem with room. |
